tagline: Baku on the Caspian — a crescent bay city of boulevards and resort capes, and the western anchor of a trans-Caspian corridor.
summary: Azerbaijan's marine-mobility heart is Baku, built around a crescent bay on the Caspian Sea, with the landmark Boulevard waterfront, the Sea Breeze resort cluster at Mardakan/Nardaran, and the industrial suburb of Sumqayit along the coast. The Caspian is a tideless, sheltered inland sea, and Baku Bay is calm, marina-rich and lined with new waterfront development. Beyond the city, the trans-Caspian crossing to Turkmenbashi and to Aktau/Kuryk in Kazakhstan is a strategic corridor. It is a bay-leisure-and-commuter market with a long-haul Quanta-LR dimension.
why_marine_mobility: Baku's geography is a calm crescent bay ringed by boulevards, resort capes and industrial suburbs, slow by the coastal road but direct by water. Navier's Pioneer II flies the bay and cape hops — the Boulevard leisure loop, the runs to Bilgah, Mardakan and Sumqayit — silent and zero-emission on the tideless Caspian, while the Quanta-LR's hybrid range opens the strategic trans-Caspian crossings to Turkmenbashi and Kazakhstan that no all-electric day-boat can reach.

demand_signals.label: Baku Boulevard & Sea Breeze
demand_signals.note: The Baku Boulevard waterfront and the Sea Breeze resort cluster at Mardakan/Nardaran anchor a high-value leisure and residential economy on a calm crescent bay.

demand_signals.label: Baku coastal suburbs
demand_signals.note: Sumqayit, Bilgah and the Absheron peninsula resorts line a coast where the road is slow but the bay is direct — commuter and leisure water demand.

demand_signals.label: Trans-Caspian corridor
demand_signals.note: The Baku (Alat) port crossings to Turkmenbashi and to Aktau/Kuryk in Kazakhstan are strategic Caspian corridors today served by slow cargo-and-rail ferries.

use_cases.body: A clean foiling bay tier around Baku — the Boulevard leisure loop and runs to the Sea Breeze resort cluster at Mardakan/Nardaran — on the calm, tideless Caspian.
Coastal commuter hops to Sumqayit and the Absheron peninsula resorts, bypassing the slow coastal road.
Strategic trans-Caspian passenger crossings to Turkmenbashi and Aktau/Kuryk on the Quanta-LR, where the hybrid range handles the long open-sea distance.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The Baku bay-and-cape mesh — the Boulevard leisure loop (~6 nm), Baku↔Bilgah (~18 nm), Baku↔Mardakan/Nardaran (~20 nm), Baku↔Sumqayit (~16 nm) — sits inside the 70 nm all-electric range on the calm, tideless Caspian off the Boulevard and Port Baku marinas.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The bay network is Pioneer II territory; the trans-Caspian crossings — Baku (Alat)↔Turkmenbashi (~150 nm) and Baku↔Aktau/Kuryk (~230–250 nm) — are long-haul Quanta-LR hybrid corridors (H2 2026+) far beyond all-electric range, where the hybrid drivetrain is essential.

signature_routes.label: Baku Boulevard ↔ Bilgah / Sea Breeze (Mardakan) (all-electric bay-and-cape run)
Baku (Alat) ↔ Aktau / Kuryk (Kazakhstan trans-Caspian corridor, Quanta-LR)

transit_planning: For the Baku International Sea Trade Port, ASCO (the Caspian Shipping Company) or a Baku waterfront developer: a clean bay tier off the Boulevard and a long-haul trans-Caspian passenger dimension on the Quanta-LR, integrated with Azerbaijan's waterfront-development and Caspian-corridor strategy.
competitive_landscape: Baku Bay has leisure boats and the Boulevard waterfront but no fast, clean, scheduled water transport; the trans-Caspian crossings run on slow cargo-and-rail ferries (ASCO). There is no foiling tier on either the bay or the corridors, leaving greenfield room on the calm Caspian.
regulatory_note: Maritime activity falls under the Baku International Sea Trade Port and the Azerbaijan Caspian Shipping Company (ASCO), with the Caspian a tideless, sheltered inland sea simplifying near-shore operation. Trans-Caspian crossings involve bilateral coordination with Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan. Azerbaijan's waterfront-development agenda supports a clean bay tier.
seasonality: The tideless Caspian gives a stable near-shore profile, with the bay calm for much of the year; the resort-and-leisure peak is the warm May–September season, while autumn and winter bring the strong Khazri north wind that can build chop, where a stabilised foiling craft has the advantage. The trans-Caspian corridors run year-round.
